answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each identity lock a refundable deposit before it can earn: at dawn of every epoch the ledger checks bonds, and any agent caught voting twice loses its stake. An attacker facing a delta between cheap talk and real locked capital must fund every fake identity, so a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds — an island of fakes collapses the moment the bond check runs, because the deposit, not the claim, is what the economy trusts.
